items.title: The derived tensor product with the quotients by the powers of an ideal agrees with the plain quotients as a pro-system
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a Noetherian ring, an ideal and a bounded complex of finite modules, the comparison between the derived tensor product with the quotients by the powers of the ideal and the plain quotients of the complex is an isomorphism of pro-objects (statement lines 29014-29023). The proof is a chain of three reductions: the quotient systems are replaced by Koszul systems, whose finite degree range makes the pro-isomorphism criterion applicable on cohomology in each degree, and the complex is then replaced by a bounded above complex of finite free modules so that the Artin-Rees consequence identifies both pro-systems with the quotients of the cohomology (proof lines 29025-29056). The degree bookkeeping and the last identification are what make the argument work. The counted span refers three times, twice to results of this chapter and once to a pro-isomorphism criterion of another chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
